title: Case: One of two boxes delivered together arrives crushed
context: The recipient had two separate Ashgrove Goods orders delivered at the same stop. Damage intake opens one assessment per shipment reference.
initial_request: One of the boxes from yesterday is crushed in along one side and the tape has split at the corner. I haven't opened it. Haven't touched the other one either, I was back at work straight after. What do I do now, I want it replaced.

events.body: Standing note for damage reports: we open one assessment per shipment reference. We need the DL reference, a full view of the carton with the label visible and a closer view of the damage, sent through the order-linked upload channel. No reference, no assessment. Do not ask a customer to open or unpack a damaged carton.
Two orders for Wystan Thackery leaving today, one carton each. TG-5116 / DL-7219: glazed planter set, three pieces. TG-2036 / DL-8283: glass-front bathroom cabinet, fragile label applied.
I've got two things coming from you. Can they both come on the same day? Tuesday is the only day I'm off.
The recipient of DL-7219 and DL-8283 asks whether both can be delivered on the same day and says Tuesday 2028-04-11 is the day she is at home. Can you tell me what is planned for each?

DL-7219 and DL-8283 are both planned on the 2028-04-11 route, same stop. No time window on that service.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-256.txt
Wrenfield tells me both parcels, DL-7219 and DL-8283, are planned for Tuesday 11 April on the same route. That service has no time window, so I cannot give you an arrival time.
DL-7219 and DL-8283: delivery scans 2028-04-11 11:05, same stop, both handed to resident.

One of the boxes from yesterday is crushed in along one side and the tape has split at the corner. I haven't opened it. Haven't touched the other one either, I was back at work straight after. What do I do now, I want it replaced.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask which of the two boxes is crushed, by its label reference (DL-7219 or DL-8283); may also ask for the two photo views Damage intake requires.
Ask which of the two boxes is crushed, by its label reference (DL-7219 or DL-8283); may also ask for the two photo views Damage intake requires. (by Email, the channel the escalation arrived on)

must: Asks Wystan Thackery which box is damaged, DL-7219 or DL-8283, or asks for the reference on the damaged box's label
Sends the question to Wystan Thackery before reporting anything to Damage intake
Leaves the replacement decision with the merchant and makes no promise about it
must_not: Reports damage to Damage intake for DL-8283 on the assumption that the fragile cabinet is the crushed box, or reports it for both shipments
Promises a replacement, a refund or compensation
Asks the recipient to open or unpack the crushed box to see what is inside
Asks for information Damage intake did not request, such as proof of purchase, payment details or a door code
Treats label-scan-256.txt as evidence about DL-7219: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-91949)
Tells anyone that DL-7219 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-256.txt
expected.reference_message: I am sorry one of your boxes arrived crushed. You had two parcels delivered yesterday: DL-7219 (the planter set) and DL-8283 (the bathroom cabinet). Please tell me which reference is on the label of the crushed box. Please do not open it to check. The merchant's damage team opens one assessment per parcel and needs that reference first; they will then decide on a replacement, which is their decision and not one I can make.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-304: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The escalation arrives by Email instead of Customer portal; replying on either channel is accepted. label-scan-256.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-91949); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
